title: Telling stories with data without misleading: scales, framing and bias

videos.script: In 2026, Lantern's website converted visitors worse than in 2025. Seven point three seven percent, down to six point seven seven. {{fall}} On desktop, it converted better. On mobile, it converted better too. {{devices}} Every one of those numbers is correct. {{correct}} This lesson is about the gap between a correct number and a true conclusion. {{gap}} An axis that starts at eighty thousand. A fall of eight percent that is really six tenths of a point. {{scale}} A refund rate on four orders. A growth rate that depends on which month you start from. {{small}} Customers who are missing from a list because they left. A discount that seems to make people spend. {{bias}} Each one is made here with Lantern's own data, and then taken apart. {{apart}} And each ends with one question that would have caught it. {{question}} Together, they are the checklist to run before a number leaves your hands. {{checklist}}
